noise_scale.quote: The noise level is defined as | \text{Noise Level}~(\%)=\frac{\mbox{var}(\text{Noise)}}{\mbox{var}(\text{Signal})}\times 100\%. | (19) Figure 2: Top: Noise identification error of modified SINDy (labeled as SINDy) and NN denoising approach by Rudy et al. [1].

noise_type.quote: Different magnitudes of Gaussian noise are added to generate the noisy training data.

noise_location.quote: In practice, noise-free measurements of \mathbf{x}(t) are not available, and only the full state noisy measurement | \mathbf{y}(t)=\mathbf{x}(t)+\mathbf{n}(t), | (4) is provided to SINDy from sensors, where \mathbf{y}(t)=[y_{1}(t),y_{2}(t),\cdots,y_{n}(t)]\in\mathbb{R}^{1\times n} is noisy measurement and \mathbf{n}(t)=[n_{1}(t),n_{2}(t),\cdots,n_{n}(t)]\in\mathbb{R}^{1\times n} is the noise added to true state.

x0.quote: The Lorenz attractor is simulated with initial condition x_{0}=[5,5,25] , T=25 , and dt=0.01 .

dt.quote: The Lorenz attractor is simulated with initial condition x_{0}=[5,5,25] , T=25 , and dt=0.01 .

t_end.quote: The Lorenz attractor is simulated with initial condition x_{0}=[5,5,25] , T=25 , and dt=0.01 .

poly_degree.quote: For modified SINDy, the library is constructed with terms up to second order (not including the constant term).

noise.quote: The time step is fixed at dt=0.01 with 10\% of Gaussian noise added to generate noisy training data.
